title: Verify all-or-nothing authorized Case discovery under late ACL provider failure
goal: Close a material read-only Case discovery authorization verification gap: a late second-Case AccessChecker error, invalid decision or cancellation must not publish a partially authorized Case catalog or private ID.
invariants: Case discovery is a read-only Class-0 projection of server-owned Case refs under CAP-INV-110; Shared owns Timeline Entry and event sources.
Catalog enumeration alone conveys no permission; each Case requires its own trusted server-derived Case read check.
An operational failure after an earlier allowed Case must not emit even a partial successful list or provider diagnostic.
No new persistence, IAM provider, Case mutation, Trace, source export, or OPEN-013 decision.
security_properties: Never disclose any Case ID from an earlier allow when a later ACL provider returns an error or unrecognized decision.
An authenticated request-derived context revoked during subsequent Case authorization must fail before response disclosure.
AccessRequest must carry server-derived tenant/environment and bind CaseID to ObjectID and the canonical Case read permission.

migration.rationale: Behavioral regression-only validation of existing read-only Case discovery; no runtime schema or persistent state.

rollback.strategy: Remove only additional Case discovery adversarial integration tests; do not change existing authorization code.
verification: Existing Case/Timeline/source owner authorization remains untouched.
The mandatory 90% security gate remains unchanged.

inputs: Full canonical CAP-INV-110 fiche and Cases-and-Evidence owner model.
Existing read-only Case discovery HTTP handler, session resolver and AccessChecker contracts.
Observed exact-head global security coverage gap on PR #131: 89.30% below mandatory 90.00%, including uncovered Case discovery late-failure branches.
outputs: Server-side Case discovery tests with late provider failure/unknown outcome and request-derived cancellation after first allowed Case.
No partial Case IDs or sensitive ACL diagnostic in any denial response.
Exact-head GitHub Actions results and non-fabricated handoff.
acceptance_tests: When first Case access is allowed and second Case provider fails, discovery returns generic 404 with no first Case leak.
When second Case provider returns an unrecognized decision, discovery fails atomically rather than treating it as allow or skip.
When authenticated request context cancels inside the second Case ACL check, discovery emits no authorized Case list.
All Case permissions use server-derived tenant/environment and exact CaseID/ObjectID binding.
Exact-head Linux Go+Node, macOS and Windows runtime CI; unchanged mandatory security coverage >=90 and negative authorization/tenant gates.

performance_budget.rationale: Retain bounded existing Case catalog size; new tests use two Cases and add no runtime work.
metrics: No new production allocations or additional permission checks per discovered Case.
Existing MaxEntries and total selector budget unchanged.

definition_of_ready: Real late ACL failure branches identified in GitHub Actions security coverage diagnostics.
Test-only contribution scoped to CAP-INV-110, no new product contract or provider implementation.
definition_of_done: Published real integration tests verify atomic refusal after a permitted first Case.
Exact published HEAD has all mandatory CI passed including unmodified 90% security floor, or stays blocked with explicit evidence.
Recoverable GitHub handoff without production/acceptance claim.
